<div class="parsedown-markdown"><div class="math-render">$$
\text{Given a function f defined in } C^{\infty}(a, b)( a \lt b ) , \text{we can expand f(x) at the point of } x_{0} :
$$</div>
<div class="math-render">$$
f(x) = f(x_0) + f'(x_0)(x - x_0) + \frac{f''(x_0)}{2!}(x - x_0)^2 +\dots, \text{ for any x in (a, b)}
$$</div>
<p>the equality above is referred to as <strong>Tayler Expansion</strong> in point <span class="math-render">$x_{0}$</span></p></div>
<div class="parsedown-markdown-end_FLAG_ZXSQ" style="display:none"></div><br>
